static_traits.name: Wei Shan
static_traits.educational_background: Graduated from an Ivy League school
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends and family to confide in, but has not yet discussed salary dissatisfaction and sense of inadequacy with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness history, never received psychotherapy before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, able to identify the 'should' tendency in own thoughts; high cooperation, Positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I believe that despite my prestigious education and financial Work, my income has not reached the level I deserve, which makes me feel dissatisfied and inadequate.
basic_info.core_demands: Setting clearer career advancement goals and breaking them into actionable small steps; discussing Career development and promotion paths with the manager, thereby improving Work satisfaction and reducing the sense of inadequacy.
growth_experiences: After graduating from an Ivy League school and entering the financial industry, felt dissatisfied and pressured from the start due to high salary expectations; this dissatisfaction and sense of inadequacy have persisted and worsened with comparisons to peers and industry standards.

Last week a colleague mentioned their bonus was significantly higher, triggering a strong sense of being undervalued and affecting mood all day, deepening the belief that 'income should highly match educational background' and dissatisfaction.

Although they have received positive feedback from superiors and several promotions, they still tend to measure success by the single indicator of salary, thereby ignoring existing achievements and the supportive work atmosphere, intensifying doubts about self-worth.

core_beliefs: My worth and success depend on salary level

special_situations.event: While discussing bonuses, a colleague reveals their bonus is markedly higher than theirs
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my income is lower than peers or colleagues, it means I am not outstanding enough and worth less
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently comparing with colleagues, trying to negotiate a raise and seek promotion to prove one's worth
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am undervalued/I am inferior to them/I should get more

special_situations.event: Discussing salary with colleagues or being triggered to talk about income and benefits at Work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: With my Ivy League educational background, I must obtain a higher salary, otherwise I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting rigid salary expectations, reinforcing 'should' standards, repeatedly thinking about income
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: With my education, I should earn more

special_situations.event: Receiving positive feedback from a supervisor or getting promoted
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only salary counts as real success and recognition; other achievements do not matter
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring and devaluing positive evidence, continuing to use salary as the sole standard for judging self-worth
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These recognitions do not count; the key is I do not earn enough

special_situations.event: Checking industry data and finding one's salary slightly below average but the gap is not large, while having a supportive Work environment and Good colleague relationships
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as it is not above average, it equals not being recognized and having no value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Selectively focusing on the lower side, ignoring the positive aspects of the Work environment and relationships, continuously worsening dissatisfaction
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is still too low; this shows I am not valued

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and fairly rewarded for my efforts (best reflected in higher salary)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing oneself not good enough, being undervalued, efforts not getting due rewards
defense_goal: Gains a sense of control and safety by maintaining high standards and 'should' rules
Relieving inner unease and Self-doubt through constant comparison and pursuing external recognition

object_relations.self_representation: An employee who is underestimated and needs to prove his value through a high salary
object_relations.object_representation: Colleagues / the organization are the authorities who judge and assign value

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When hearing colleagues talk about wages or bonuses, or being asked to see their own achievements and positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing others' statements as a negation of self-worth or inadequacy (being undervalued, not recognized)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Cites industry data or market differences in an objective, calm tone, emphasizing logic and facts, weakening or avoiding expression of emotions such as shame and loss.

manifestations: Measures success and self-worth by the single indicator of salary, ignoring positive feedback and promotions, and a supportive work environment
outcomes: Persistent dissatisfaction and sense of inadequacy

manifestations: Bound by the inner rule 'I should earn more', finding it hard to accept real differences and diverse standards
outcomes: Decreased flexibility in career choices and paths

manifestations: Although having friends' and family's support, not yet sharing salary dissatisfaction and inferiority with them
outcomes: Bearing emotions alone, Increased subjective sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Frequently using the self-Demand 'I should earn more'
Equating elite-school education and high salary as the standard that must be achieved

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeatedly reproaching herself 'I am not good enough'
After comparing with colleagues, more reserved and sensitive in interpersonal interaction

positive_force: Ivy League education and financial industry experience provide resources for Career development
Has received positive feedback from superiors and several promotions; has objective evidence of being recognized
Strongly supportive Work environment, Good relationships with colleagues
Has proactively negotiated a raise and sought promotion; has an action tendency
Actively seeks psychological counseling, positive attitude, willing to change
negative_force: Excessively relies on salary as external validation to assess self-worth
Frequently comparing with peers, reinforcing the sense of inadequacy
Rigid 'should' rules lead to unrealistic goals and expectations
Tending to negate positive evidence, focusing on the negative (salary)
Excessive focus on salary affects leisure and relationships, lowering job satisfaction

target_behavior.behavior: Excessively focuses on salary and repeatedly compares with peers, with self-deprecation and rumination
antecedent: Discussing salary or bonuses with colleagues
Checking industry salary data and peer comparisons
Thinks of her Ivy League educational background and sets high expectations accordingly
After receiving positive feedback or a promotion, still checks the salary and feels a sense of disparity
target_behavior.core_reason: Directly equates self-worth with salary level, internalizes the rigid rule 'I should earn more', and relies on external salary as the source of validation of worth
target_behavior.function: Seeking external recognition and certainty to relieve Anxiety and shame about 'not being good enough/being undervalued'; hoping to bring about raises or promotions through comparison and pressuring behaviors
target_behavior.consequence: Intensifying persistent dissatisfaction and sense of inadequacy, affecting interactions with colleagues, Difficulty relaxing and enjoying interests, Decline in job satisfaction
